issues.detail: The Greek 'αυτω' (to him) refers to the person who spoke/commanded, while 'αυτον' (him) in the final clause refers back to that same person. The Vietnamese translation uses 'nó' (it/him - informal/low status) for the second instance and 'Ngài' (He/Lord - high status) for the third. This creates a contradiction in the identity of the person being betrayed; the Greek implies the same person is being given silver and then handed over, whereas the Vietnamese suggests two different people or a confusing shift in status.
